investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-14T20:40–20:47Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable nodes for a new kata peer-pod — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState are all missing), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the Remote Agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no existing pod can be evicted to free capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are ineligible by affinity. The pod remained unscheduled for ~143 s until the eval timed out, so the agent VM was never created and no contract evidence was produced.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots on those nodes, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' may have had labels removed, changed, or the pod spec's affinity rules may have become overly restrictive, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying VM capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, preventing new scheduling. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1883) but a prior failed cleanup could leave pods running.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata-eligible nodes may have been provisioned with a kata.peerpods.io/vm limit that is too low for concurrent eval and production workloads, and no autoscaling or node-pool expansion is configured for this resource type.

If a subsequent eval run immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient and capacity was freed between runs, weakening the exhaustion hypothesis.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods are found on the 2 eligible nodes, the resource limit itself may be set to zero or the extended resource may not be registered on those nodes, pointing to a node configuration or device-plugin issue rather than workload-driven exhaustion.

If the history shows this is the first-ever run (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null), a passing run in a different environment or with a freshly provisioned cluster would indicate the production cluster was never correctly sized for this workload, not that a regression occurred.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-14T20:40–20:47Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable nodes for a new kata peer-pod — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState are all missing), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the Remote Agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and "No preemption victims found" confirms that no existing pod can be evicted to free capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes are ineligible by affinity. The pod remained unscheduled for ~143 s until the eval timed out, so the agent VM was never created and no contract evidence was produced.

Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' may have had labels removed, changed, or the pod spec's affinity rules may have become overly restrictive, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity pressure.

The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1883) but a prior failed cleanup could leave pods running.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-14 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~142–143 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present; this is an eval-level failure.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes — concurrent or lingering peer-pod VMs from prior eval runs, other workloads, or leaked agent instances have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes — the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes), so the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to those 2 nodes before capacity is even considered.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs from previous eval runs not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper — if prior agent instances were not fully terminated, their VM slots would remain allocated and unavailable for new pods.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler not configured or unable to provision additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time — the preemption message confirms no autoscaling or preemption path was available.

[Lower likelihood] A recent infrastructure change reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes or lowered the per-node VM quota — no suspect changes are present in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges to support this hypothesis.
